# v0.10.0b3 — Hardening of the single service

- Breaking: the service image runs as its own user (UID 10001) instead of root and the service gives up every capability at its start. A standalone container needs a data directory that user can write and, for USB, the adapter's group (`--group-add`); see the standalone guide. The Home Assistant app needs nothing: it stays root for Supervisor's data, without any capability.
- Serial and Modbus RTU over TCP: an answer that arrived after its request had timed out was taken for the answer to the next read, which could show a charging wallbox as idle. The service now lets the line fall silent after a request without a usable answer, and a line that does not answer at all costs a poll two register blocks instead of all of them.
- A waiting pause, lock or withdrawn release is no longer lost to a failed poll, a lost reply, a current change or a goal stop. It is replaced only by what overrides it; a command that would have to wait itself is refused instead of taking its place.
- Error-200 recovery runs to its end while the service cannot save its state; a command the wallbox received but the service could not save is answered as such (`intent_not_saved`).
- Home Assistant: sign-in, calendar, departure-time and target-time messages are translated, diagnostics work for an entry whose setup never finished, and a disabled entry takes its repairs along.
- Privacy and legal texts were checked again (VIN pseudonym, rounded coordinates, the Waveshare finding stated as this project's own test).

Update the app and the integration to **0.10.0b3** together. Charging with a car is not yet tested on this build.
